worldcup-1930.summary: The very first tournament, held in Montevideo, Uruguay, where the hosts beat neighbouring Argentina 4–2 in the final.
facts: There was no qualifying; only the 13 nations that accepted invitations took part.
It was timed to mark the 100th anniversary of the host nation's first constitution.

worldcup-1934.summary: Held in Mussolini's Italy, where the hosts beat Czechoslovakia after extra time in the final in Rome.
facts: It's the only tournament the reigning champions didn't enter.
It was the first edition held in Europe and the first to use qualifying rounds to pick the 16 finalists.

worldcup-1938.summary: Held in France, where Italy beat Hungary in the final in Paris to become the first team to retain the title.
facts: The Dutch East Indies became the first Asian team to play at the finals.
No World Cup was held for the next 12 years.

worldcup-1950.summary: Held in Brazil, where Uruguay beat the hosts 2–1 in the decisive last match at the Maracanã to take the title.
facts: Instead of a knockout final, a final-round league decided the champion.
It resumed after a 12-year break caused by the Second World War.

worldcup-1954.summary: Held in Switzerland and remembered for the “Miracle of Bern,” when West Germany came back to beat the unbeatable Hungarians 3–2 in the final.
facts: Hungary had thrashed West Germany 8–3 in the group stage.
South Korea, playing in its first finals, lost 9–0 to Hungary.

worldcup-1958.summary: Held in Sweden, where Brazil, led by 17-year-old Pelé, beat the hosts in the final to win their first title.
facts: France's Just Fontaine scored 13 goals, setting the record for a single tournament.
It was the first time a team from South America won a tournament held in Europe.

worldcup-1962.summary: Held in Chile, where Garrincha carried an injury-hit Brazil without Pelé to a second straight title.
facts: Brazil beat Czechoslovakia 3–1 in the final.
A brawl between Chile and Italy went down in history as the “Battle of Santiago.”

worldcup-1966.summary: Held in England, where the hosts beat West Germany for their first title after a disputed extra-time goal in the Wembley final.
facts: World Cup Willie, a lion, became the tournament's first official mascot.
It's also remembered for North Korea's run to the quarterfinals.

worldcup-1970.summary: Held in Mexico, where Pelé's Brazil beat Italy 4–1 and kept the Jules Rimet Trophy for good with a third title.
facts: Matches were broadcast live by satellite, some of them in color for the first time.
Yellow cards and substitutions were used for the first time.

worldcup-1974.summary: Held in West Germany, where the hosts beat Johan Cruyff's “Total Football” Netherlands in the final in Munich.
facts: The Dutch went ahead from a penalty two minutes into the final but lost 2–1.
The current FIFA World Cup Trophy was awarded for the first time.

worldcup-1978.summary: Held in Argentina under military rule, where the hosts beat the Netherlands 3–1 after extra time for their first title.
facts: The Netherlands finished runner-up for the second tournament in a row.
Kempes scored twice in the final and finished as top scorer.

worldcup-1982.summary: Held in Spain, where Italy beat West Germany 3–1 in the final in Madrid for their third title.
facts: The finals expanded to 24 teams for the first time.
Paolo Rossi finished as top scorer with six goals.

worldcup-1986.summary: Moved to Mexico, the first country to host twice, after Colombia pulled out, and won by Maradona's Argentina.
facts: Both the “Hand of God” and the “Goal of the Century” came in the quarterfinal against England.
South Korea returned to the finals for the first time in 32 years.

worldcup-1990.summary: Held in Italy, where West Germany beat Argentina 1–0 in the final in Rome for their third title.
facts: At 2.21 goals per match, it was the lowest-scoring tournament ever.
Cameroon became the first team from Africa to reach the quarterfinals.

worldcup-1994.summary: Held in the United States, where Brazil returned to the top after 24 years and became the first nation to win four titles.
facts: For the first time, the final went to a penalty shootout, which ended with Baggio's miss.
More than 3.5 million spectators attended, setting an attendance record for the tournament.

worldcup-1998.summary: Held in France, where the hosts beat Brazil 3–0 in the final in Saint-Denis for their first title.
facts: The finals expanded to 32 teams for the first time.
Zidane headed in two goals from corner kicks in the final.

worldcup-2002.summary: Co-hosted by South Korea and Japan as the first edition in Asia, with Brazil winning a fifth title in the final in Yokohama.
facts: South Korea reached the semifinals under coach Guus Hiddink.
Ronaldo, with two goals in the final, finished as top scorer with eight.

worldcup-2006.summary: Held in Germany and remembered for Zidane's sending-off for headbutting Materazzi in the final in Berlin.
facts: The final was decided on penalties after a 1–1 draw.
Italy won its fourth title.

worldcup-2010.summary: The first edition in Africa, held in South Africa, where Spain won their first title in the final in Johannesburg.
facts: Paul the Octopus correctly predicted all seven of Germany's matches as well as the final.
For the first time, the hosts were knocked out in the group stage.

worldcup-2014.summary: Held in Brazil, where the hosts collapsed 7–1 to Germany in the semifinal and Germany went on to win the final in Rio.
facts: Goal-line technology was used at a World Cup for the first time.
Mario Götze's extra-time goal gave Germany a 1–0 win over Argentina in the final.

worldcup-2018.summary: Held in Russia, where France beat Croatia 4–2 in the final in Moscow for their second title.
facts: It was the first edition in which referees could change decisions using video review.
South Korea beat Germany 2–0 in the group stage.

worldcup-2022.summary: The first edition in the Middle East, held in Qatar, where Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3–3 final.
facts: To avoid the heat, it kicked off in November for the first time.
Messi lifted the trophy for the first time at his fifth World Cup.

worldcup-2026.summary: Co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico with 48 teams, and won by Spain over Argentina in the final.
facts: The number of matches grew from 64 to 104, played across 16 cities.
It was the first edition with three co-hosts and the first with 48 teams.
